newsitem.title: USA: Mideast summit to operate under news blackout.
newsitem.headline: Mideast summit to operate under news blackout.

text.p: The United States intends to impose a news blackout on a Middle East summit starting on Tuesday while hammering out an Israeli-Palestinian accord to end an explosion of violence, officials said.
"The idea is for there to be no statements for 24 hours until the conclusion of the summit," said an Israeli official travelling with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to the White House summit.

A U.S. official said the meetings would take place under "Dayton rules" -- a reference to the intensive closed-door U.S.-sponsored negotiations in Dayton, Ohio, that led to last year's Bosnian peace accord.

U.S. President Bill Clinton will host the Middle East summit attended by Netanyahu, Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Jordan's King Hussein. Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak, locked in a war of words with Israel over the slow pace of peace, turned down an invitation to join.
Israeli-Palestinian violence last week, coinciding with the 100-day anniversary of Netanyahu's right-wing government, claimed the lives of 70 Palestinians and Israelis.
